# New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryCheck

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a check for a network discovery rule.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryCheck [-Type] <ZabbixNetworkDiscoveryCheckType> [-Key <string>] [-SnmpOid <string>] [-SnmpCommunity <string>] [-SnmpSecurityName <string>] [-SnmpSecurityLevel <ZabbixSnmpSecurityLevel>] [-SnmpAuthenticationPassphrase <SecureString>] [-SnmpAuthenticationProtocol <ZabbixSnmpAuthenticationProtocol>] [-SnmpPrivacyPassphrase <SecureString>] [-SnmpPrivacyProtocol <ZabbixSnmpPrivacyProtocol>] [-SnmpContextName <string>] [-Port <int>] [-Ports <string>] [-Unique] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A network discovery check is one probe a network discovery rule runs on each address: ICMP ping, a service port such as SSH or HTTP, a Zabbix agent key or an SNMP OID. The New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryCheck cmdlet writes it as a typed ZabbixNetworkDiscoveryCheckRequest, which the -Check of New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule and Set-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule take as it is, alone or in an array. The SNMPv3 passphrases are kept but not shown by the default view. Nothing is sent to the server.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build an ICMP ping check

```powershell
New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryCheck -Type Icmp
```

A check is a hashtable of the dcheck's wire fields (type, key_, ports, uniq...); nothing is sent until a discovery rule is created or changed with it.

### Example 2: Build an agent check that identifies the device

```powershell
New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryCheck -Type ZabbixAgent -Key 'system.hostname' -Port 10050 -Unique
```

-Key is the item key the agent answers; -Unique makes this check's value decide whether two discovered devices are the same host (uniq). -Port is the agent's port; -Ports takes a list or range instead.

### Example 3: Build an SNMPv2c check and a TCP port check

```powershell
New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryCheck -Type SnmpV2c -SnmpOid '1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0' -SnmpCommunity '{$SNMP_COMMUNITY}' -Port 161
New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryCheck -Type Tcp -Ports '22,80,443'
```

An SNMP check takes -SnmpOid and -SnmpCommunity (a macro works as well as a literal); -Ports on a TCP check lists the ports to probe.

### Example 4: Create a discovery rule from the checks

```powershell
$checks = @(
    New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryCheck -Type Icmp
    New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryCheck -Type ZabbixAgent -Key 'system.hostname' -Port 10050 -Unique
)
New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule -Name 'Local network' -IPRange '192.0.2.1-254' -Check $checks -Status Disabled | Out-Null
Get-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule -Name 'Local network' -SelectNetworkDiscoveryChecks |
    ForEach-Object Checks | Select-Object Type, Key, Ports, Unique
```

New-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule -Check binds the hashtables directly, alone or in an array. The rule is created disabled here, so the server does not scan the range yet.
